# Mindroot

Mindroot is a free, open-source mind-mapping app. It runs as a desktop app on macOS, Windows and Linux, and as a web app at https://mindroot.app/app/. It is local-first: maps are plain files on the user's disk, and the app needs no account and no cloud service. It is keyboard-first: a user can build a full map without the mouse. The license is MIT.

- Website: https://mindroot.app
- Web version (the app in the browser): https://mindroot.app/app/
- Source code: https://github.com/falhad/mindroot
- Download: https://github.com/falhad/mindroot/releases/latest
- Author: Farhad (GitHub: falhad)

## Who it is for

- People who want a fast mind-mapping tool that works offline and keeps data on their own computer.
- Developers and writers who prefer the keyboard and plain files, and who already use Git.
- People who write in Persian, Arabic or Hebrew and need a correct right-to-left layout.
- People who look for a free, open-source alternative to a paid or cloud-based mind-mapping service.

## Main features

- Infinite canvas with six layouts: mind map (both sides), right tree, left tree, org chart down, org chart up, radial.
- Keyboard-first editing: Tab adds a child idea, Enter adds a sibling, the arrow keys move, Ctrl/Cmd+K opens a command palette with all commands.
- Each idea can have a colour, shape, icon, tags, a due date, a checklist, attached files, and a link to another map.
- Notes on each idea in Markdown, with code highlighting and LaTeX formulas.
- Cross-links between ideas, groups, summary brackets, floating ideas and sticky notes.
- Outline view (edit the map as a list), focus mode (work on one branch), and presentation mode (one idea or one branch at a time).
- A library for all maps: search in titles and idea text, stars, tags, trash, templates, and a tasks page with the open tasks of all maps.
- Three line styles, six colour themes, light and dark.
- Right-to-left maps: Persian, Arabic and Hebrew maps mirror the whole layout. The Vazirmatn font is bundled and embedded in exports.
- Compare two maps, or two versions of one map.
- Quick capture (desktop): a system-wide shortcut puts a thought into an Inbox map.

## Data and privacy

- No account, no sign-up, no cloud storage.
- Desktop: each map is one JSON Lines file in a local folder ("vault"). Files are written atomically.
- Web version: maps are stored in the browser (IndexedDB) and are not sent to a server. The website counts visits with Cloudflare Web Analytics, which sets no cookies.
- The desktop app sends no data unless the user turns on Git sync, live collaboration, the AI assistant or the update check.

## Sync and collaboration

- Git sync: the user points the app at their own private Git repository (for example on GitHub, GitLab or a private server). Maps sync between computers. When two computers edit the same map, Mindroot merges the changes idea by idea, not line by line, so both edits survive.
- History: restore an old version of a map, or one idea from it (desktop, with Git sync).
- Live collaboration: several people edit one map in real time through a small relay server that the user runs (Node, Docker). There is no hosted collaboration service.

## AI assistant

- Optional. The user brings their own API key for an OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic-compatible service (for example OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, or a custom address).
- Commands: make a new map from a topic or a pasted text; expand an idea; find what is missing in a branch; summarize a branch into notes; rewrite the text of an idea.
- Only the text that the user typed, or the selected branch, is sent to the service the user configured.
- Mindroot has no AI service of its own and adds no cost.

## Import and export

- Import: Markdown and indented outlines, FreeMind (.mm), OPML, XMind, Obsidian canvas, Mindroot JSON, and generic JSON with text and children.
- Export: JSON, Markdown, OPML, PNG, SVG, PDF (vector with selectable text, or image), and a single-file web page that opens in any browser.

## Plugins

Git sync, the AI assistant and live collaboration are plugins on a public plugin API. Other people can write plugins that add commands, header chips, settings panels and event listeners. Plugins install from a gallery.

## Platforms and install

- Web: https://mindroot.app/app/ (no install). Git sync and quick capture need the desktop app.
- macOS: .dmg for Apple Silicon and for Intel.
- Windows: .exe installer or .msi.
- Linux: AppImage, .deb, .rpm (x86-64).
- The installers are not code-signed yet, so the system shows a warning at the first start. On macOS: System Settings → Privacy & Security → "Open Anyway", or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Mindroot.app`. On Windows: "More info" → "Run anyway".
- The desktop app updates itself; updates are signature-checked.

## Technology

Tauri 2 (Rust) for the desktop shell, React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind 4 and Zustand. Tauri uses the system web view, so the macOS and Windows installers are about 5 MB and the app starts fast.

## Known limits

- No mobile app yet. The web version works on a phone browser.
- No public share links. The single-file web page export is the closest today.
- Installers are not code-signed yet.
- In the web version, some AI services refuse requests that come directly from a browser; the desktop app has no such limit.
- No Linux build for ARM yet.

## Common questions

**Is Mindroot free?** Yes. It is free and open source (MIT). There is no paid plan.

**Does it need an account?** No.

**Where are my maps?** Desktop: in a folder on your disk, one file for each map. Web: in your browser's storage.

**Can I use it offline?** Yes, with the desktop app: it works fully offline. The web version needs a connection to load the page.

**How do I sync between two computers?** Turn on Git sync and give it a private Git repository that you own.

**Can I open my XMind or FreeMind maps?** Yes. Import supports XMind, FreeMind (.mm), OPML, Markdown and Obsidian canvas.

**Does it work for Persian, Arabic or Hebrew?** Yes. Right-to-left maps mirror the full layout, and exports embed the font.

**How does it compare with cloud mind-mapping services?** Mindroot stores data locally in an open format, has no subscription, and syncs through the user's own Git repository. It has no hosted real-time service and no mobile app.
